threads.body: The new same-class suppression depends on `actualFactoryClass`, but it is assigned (line 47) only *after* `installed.compareAndSet(false, true)` (line 34) opens the install gate. A second install of the same factory class that loses the CAS during the brief window before line 47 runs will read `actualFactoryClass == null`, so `incomingClass.equals(actualFactoryClass)` is false and the "Multiple application logger implementations were provided" warning is still emitted — the exact symptom this PR aims to remove. In a Spring Boot app both install paths can fire (the SLF4J `LoggerFactory` exit path and the `LoggingApplicationListener` exit path), potentially from different threads, so this race is reachable. Consider publishing the winning factory class atomically with claiming the gate — e.g., replace the `installed` AtomicBoolean with an `AtomicReference<Class<? extends InternalLogger.Factory>>` and CAS `null` → `incomingClass`; losers then compare against its always-non-null value — so the recorded class is visible to any thread that loses the race.

replies.body: Good catch. Fixed by replacing the separate AtomicBoolean + volatile field approach with a single AtomicReference<Class<?>>. The CAS is now null to incomingClass, so the winning class is stored atomically as part of claiming the gate. Any thread that loses the race immediately reads a non-null value from installedFactoryClass.get() — the window is gone entirely.

replies.body:
Good catch, you're right — comparing classes was the wrong layer here, especially since the bridge builds a new instance every call anyway.

Moved the dedup up into Slf4jApplicationLoggerBridge#install() with a static AtomicBoolean, so it only ever hands off the first instance regardless of how many times slf4j/Spring Boot's logging listener fires. ApplicationLoggerFactory is back to the original plain AtomicBoolean check, since a second install() there now really does mean a different implementation was provided.

Also added an assertion in the fork-based ApplicationLoggerInstrumentationTest that the warning never shows up in the TestSpringApp output.

@trask could you take another look?

threads.body: The PR description and the actual code changes describe two different implementations. The description says the fix replaces an `AtomicBoolean installed` gate and a `volatile actualFactoryClass` field with a single `AtomicReference<Class<? extends InternalLogger.Factory>>` in `ApplicationLoggerFactory.java`, and adds a `shouldIgnoreSubsequentInstallationsOfSameClass` test plus `FirstFactory`/`SecondFactory` classes in `ApplicationLoggerFactoryTest.java`. However, this diff instead *adds* an `AtomicBoolean installed` gate in `Slf4jApplicationLoggerBridge.install()` (so `installApplicationLogger` runs at most once) and adds an assertion to `ApplicationLoggerInstrumentationTest.java`; `ApplicationLoggerFactory.java` and `ApplicationLoggerFactoryTest.java` are not modified at all. The implemented approach looks correct, but the description is stale and should be updated to match the actual changes to avoid confusing reviewers and future maintainers.

replies.body: Good catch — the description was left over from an earlier iteration of this fix. Updated it to match the current implementation (dedup in `Slf4jApplicationLoggerBridge#install()` via a static `AtomicBoolean`).
